post.description:
Creates a new payment request.

Supports two flows in a single endpoint:
- **Standalone payment** — omit `tab_id` and `payment_type`; behaves like v2.
- **Pay at Table (PAT)** — supply `tab_id` (the tab to link the payment to) and
  `payment_type` (`FULL` or `SPLIT`). `payment_type` is
  required whenever `tab_id` is present.

**Required Scopes (one of the following):**

- `payment_requests` (returned via the register API: `POST /poslink/v1/epos/register`)
- `default_access` (deprecated, will be removed in the future; included for backward compatibility with existing integrations)

get.description:
Returns tabs for the specified store, cursor-paginated.

Supports optional filters:
- `status`: repeatable. When omitted, defaults to active tabs only
  (`OPEN`, `PAYING`, `PAUSED`). To include archived tabs, pass
  `status=COMPLETED` and/or `status=CLOSED` explicitly.
- `merchant_reference`: merchant-assigned reference. Unique per store, so the
  filtered response will contain at most one tab.

post.description:
Terminal initiates a payment intent for a tab. The tab transitions to
`PAYING` if it is in `OPEN` or `PAUSED`; PAYING tabs are no-op idempotent.
On a `PAUSED → PAYING` transition POSLink auto-emits a `TAB_RESUMED` SSE
event before the `PAY_REQUEST`. The ePOS then calls POST /v3/payment-requests
(with tab_id and payment_type) to materialise the payment. Supports FULL and
SPLIT payment types with CARD or CASH methods.

get.description:
Returns the store's payments and refunds, newest first.

**What to send:** the store you want to look at. You can optionally narrow the results by terminal, status, type (sale or refund), or a date range, and page through large result sets using the page size and starting position.

**What you get back:** a list where each entry shows the amount, whether it was a sale or a refund, its current status, and — where relevant — the reason behind that status (for example, why a payment was declined or cancelled). The response also tells you how many results match in total so you can page through them.

**Required Scopes (one of the following):**

- `payment_requests` (returned via the register API: `POST /poslink/v1/epos/register`)
- `default_access` (deprecated, will be removed in the future; included for backward compatibility with existing integrations)

post.summary: Register ePOS application and retrieve M2M client credentials
post.description:
### No Permission Required - This is an endpoint that does not require permission
---

This API registers an ePOS application and returns M2M (machine-to-machine) client credentials.
The endpoint returns OAuth client credentials based on the provided store_id and epos_external_id.
The client credentials can be used to obtain M2M access tokens for subsequent API calls.

**Authentication:**

This endpoint requires a user JWT token (not M2M credentials). The user must have access to the specified store.

**Returned Scopes:**

The response includes OAuth scopes that define which APIs can be accessed with the returned M2M credentials:
- `payment_requests`: Required to create, list, and cancel or update payment requests.
- `payment_requests/id`: Required to retrieve and follow an individual payment request.
- `stores/id/terminals`: Required to list stores and their terminals.
- `refunds`: Required for refund operations

**Using the Returned Credentials:**

The returned client credentials are used to obtain an M2M access token via OAuth2 client credentials flow. The access token must include the scopes returned in this response to call the corresponding APIs.

**Idempotency Behavior:**
- The API is idempotent based on the composite key: (partner_id from JWT, store_id, epos_external_id)
- The response body structure is identical for both status codes, containing the same client credentials.

**Idempotency Key:** (partner_id, store_id, epos_external_id)

patch.description:
### No Permission Required - This is an endpoint that does not require permission
---

This API call is used to request the cancellation of a payment request by setting its status to `CANCELLING`.

This call is a *request* to cancel, not a confirmation that the payment was cancelled. A successful (`200`) response means the cancellation request has been accepted and the payment request has moved to `CANCELLING` — it does not mean the payment has been cancelled.

Whether the payment is actually cancelled depends on how far the terminal has progressed:

- If the terminal has not yet started processing the payment, the terminal cancels the payment request and its status becomes `CANCELLED` with a status reason of `CANCELLED_BY_EPOS`.
- If the terminal has already started processing the payment, the cancellation cannot be applied and the payment continues to its final status (`SUCCESSFUL` or `FAILED`), which overrides `CANCELLING`.

To confirm the outcome, keep following the payment request’s status updates until it reaches a final state. The payment is only cancelled when the status is `CANCELLED`; a final state of `SUCCESSFUL` or `FAILED` means the cancellation did not take effect.

**Required Scopes (one of the following):**

- `payment_requests` (returned via the register API: `POST /poslink/v1/epos/register`)
- `default_access` (deprecated, will be removed in the future; included for backward compatibility with existing integrations)

parameters.name: payment-request-id
parameters.description: The ID assigned to the payment request

200.description: Cancellation request accepted. The payment request has moved to `CANCELLING`; this does not confirm the payment was cancelled. Follow the status updates until a final state (`CANCELLED`, `SUCCESSFUL`, or `FAILED`) to determine the outcome.

value.description: ePos unable to cancel payment request, As it has already completed
ePos unable to cancel payment request, transaction already in failed status
ePos unable to cancel payment request, transaction already in cancelled status

get.summary: Follow a payment or refund live
get.description:
Returns a single payment or refund and then keeps delivering its status changes as they happen, so you can show the customer live progress on screen.

**What to send:** the identifier of the payment or refund you want to follow.

**What you get back:** first the full details — the amount, whether it is a sale or a refund, its current status, and, where relevant, the reason behind that status. After that, you keep receiving updates as the status changes (for example, waiting for the card, then the final result). Once it reaches a final outcome — successful, failed, or cancelled — the final details are sent and the connection closes. If it is already finished when you ask, you get the full details once and the connection closes straight away.

**Required Scopes (one of the following):**

- `payment_requests/id` (returned via the register API: `POST /poslink/v1/epos/register`)
- `default_access` (deprecated, will be removed in the future; included for backward compatibility with existing integrations)

delete.description:
Soft-deletes a tab by setting its status to CLOSED. The tab record is retained.
Allowed source states: `OPEN`, `COMPLETED`, `PAUSED`. Closing a `PAYING` tab
is rejected because a transaction is mid-flight; drive it to a stable state
first (resume or pause). Closing a `PAUSED` tab is allowed — if a late
payment-completed event lands on the now-CLOSED tab, the credit is logged
and counted via `eposconnect.tabs.credit.on_closed_tab.count` for ops
visibility (no data recovery). Already-CLOSED tabs are rejected — the
second close is treated as an error rather than an idempotent no-op.

get.summary: Stream tab events for a store
get.description:
Streams real-time tab events for a store using Server-Sent Events (SSE).

Event types: SHOW_BILL_REQUEST, PAY_REQUEST, TAB_PAYMENT_STATUS_PROGRESS,
TAB_PAYMENT_COMPLETED, TAB_PAUSED, TAB_RESUMED, TAB_COMPLETED, TAB_BILL_HIDDEN.

Each event frame carries:
- `event:` line — the event type (matches the JSON `event_type` discriminator).
- `id:` line — a per-store monotonic event id used for `Last-Event-ID` reconnection.
- `data:` line — a flat JSON object with `event_type`, `tab_id`, `merchant_reference`,
  and event-specific fields.

Connection behaviour:
- The server emits a `:keepalive` SSE comment every ~20 seconds. ePOS clients should
  reconnect if they don't receive one within 60 seconds.
- The server closes the connection after ~10 minutes of no real events (heartbeats
  don't count) so reconnects redistribute across replicas. ePOS should auto-reconnect.
- On reconnect, send a `Last-Event-ID` header. POSLink replays missed events from a
  short-lived 5-minute buffer.
- Out-of-window reconnect: if the buffer is empty/expired, the server attaches the
  stream silently with no replay. The ePOS MUST detect gaps by checking that the
  first event id received is `LastEventId + 1`; if it jumps, call
  `GET /poslink/v1/tabs/{tab_id}` to resync state for any affected tabs.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store identifier

TAB_RESUMED.summary: POSLink auto-resumed a paused tab on POST /pay

Creates a receipt print job by either:
 - Sending a JSON payload that describes the receipt content to be rendered by the service; or
 - Uploading a pre-rendered receipt image via multipart/form-data.

 On success, a new receipt job is created and the response contains the unique receipt_id,
 initial status (NOT_PRINTED), and creation timestamp. Clients can then subscribe to status updates via the SSE endpoint or poll for the result.

 Content types:
 - application/json
 - multipart/form-data (fields: store_id, terminal_id, image)

 Response: 201 Created with a JSON body containing identifiers and initial status.

get.summary: Get receipt print job with real-time updates
get.description:
Streams real-time updates for a receipt print job using Server‑Sent Events (SSE) with content type text/event-stream.

Each message in the stream is an SSE event with:
- data: a JSON object with receipt status fields (no formal schema available for SSE payload)
- a blank line terminates each event frame

Semantics:
- The stream emits receipt status updates as they occur.
- When the receipt reaches a final status (for example, PRINTED or FAILED), a last event is sent and the stream is closed.
- If the receipt is already final when requested, a single event is sent and the connection is closed immediately.

Possible statuses:
- NOT_PRINTED
- ENQUEUED
- PRINTING
- PRINTED
- FAILED
- UNKNOWN

Possible status reasons:
- TIMEOUT
- BUSY
- OUT_OF_PAPER
- OVERHEATED
- COVER_OPEN
- LOW_BATTERY
- OTHER

Connection behavior:
- The server may close the connection after approximately one minute of inactivity; clients should reconnect if updates are still expected.

Wire example:
data: {"receipt_id":"...","status":"PRINTED","status_reason":null,"updated_at":"2025-09-10T12:30:45Z"}

Note: The response schema below describes the structure of the JSON object placed in the SSE data field, not the SSE framing itself.

CreatePaymentRequestV3.description: Request to create a new payment request. Supports standalone payments (SALE or REFUND) and Pay at Table payments (SALE only, when tab_id is provided). See transaction_type for how to request a standalone unreferenced refund.

transaction_type.description:
The transaction type of this request.
- `SALE`: a standard card-present payment (customer pays the merchant).
- `REFUND`: a standalone, unreferenced card-present refund (money returned to the customer's card with no original transaction to reference). The customer taps their card at the terminal; a new gateway transaction is created. `REFUND` is only valid for standalone requests — it is rejected with HTTP 422 when `tab_id` is present, because Pay at Table supports `SALE` only.

merchant_reference.description: The merchant reference for this payment request. Must be a unique reference that can be used to uniquely identify this payment.

scopes.description:
OAuth client scopes granted to the M2M client credentials.
These scopes define the permissions available for subsequent API calls.

The following scopes are returned:
- `payment_requests`: Access to payment requests endpoints (list operations)
- `payment_requests/id`: Access to individual payment request endpoints (by ID)
- `stores/id/terminals`: Access to store terminals endpoints
- `refunds`: Access to refunds endpoints

authorisation.description:
Given a valid access token, you can now use a Bearer Token to authenticate your requests.
To do so you have to preface your access token with Bearer and send it in the HTTP Authorization header.
It should look something like this: `Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>`
